source_text.body:
Build and test an image editor with agent-driven headless GUI
A developer had Opus build an image editor and a Sonnet subagent test it via a headless sway setup with scripted mouse and keyboard input, catching most bugs; manual checks were still needed.
·
Nov 17, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
CL
Claude
What they did
The developer hand-wrote scripts so the agent could drive the app headlessly: a headless sway instance, a daemon using Wayland virtual keyboard and mouse protocols via a unix socket, and bash glue. Commands (start, screenshot, mouse move/click, type) were documented in claude.md. Opus built the editor; a Sonnet subagent did interactive testing. The developer specified how each tool and panel should work.
How it went
Testing was mostly automatic and Sonnet caught most bugs itself. The developer still did a cursory manual check, since headless sway differs from a real desktop environment with KDE's platform theme.
Worth knowing
Scripted input mocking was far more reliable than the accessibility API route (pyatspi2) tried first; a Sonnet subagent also cut cost and avoids inheriting Opus's long context.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Build a small [type of GUI app, e.g. image editor] in this folder using [language/toolkit]. Then set up a headless display environment, such as a headless Wayland compositor, and have a separate subagent test the app by scripting mouse and keyboard input and taking screenshots. Fix every bug the tester finds, repeat until a full test pass finds no new problems, and give me a list of things you could not verify so I can check them by hand.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50533409
